summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, venous stasis ulcers, chronic pancreatitis, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for persistent left lower extremity cellulitis that failed outpatient treatment with minocycline. She presented with severe pain, swelling, spreading erythema, and fever. IV vancomycin was initiated empirically due to prior MRSA history and lack of response. Imaging ruled out osteomyelitis and DVT. Wound culture identified methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, prompting a switch to oral clindamycin. She developed non-allergic hives during admission, managed supportively. Her infection improved clinically, with reduced erythema and normalizing labs. She was discharged home on clindamycin, with instructions to continue chronic medications, use ACE wraps, and follow up with her primary care provider.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Spinal stenosis, lumbar region, without neurogenic claudication
Unspecified hereditary and idiopathic peripheral neuropathy
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
